title: Joining Sabby Lewis and moving to Boston
summary: He met Sabby Lewis's band at Kelly's Stable, replaced the bassist leaving for the Navy, and went to Boston for what became 18 years.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Then when did you go to Boston?

Well, then, right, right after I closed at Jimmy Ryan's, and, uh, then it was during the war then. So this fellow, Sabie Lewis, from Boston, had a very fine little eight piece swinging band. They were all fine musicians. They played a lot of modern and good swing music, see. So, I met him, it was my closing week. We was one block apart. He was at Kelly's stable, and, and I was down to Ryan, see. So, I passed by there, I heard a little band swinging, so I walked in. Kelly said, we were always dropping different clubs when you were around the streets, see. So, I slept a long time. So the guys, they were all looking at me, and that. So, then when they come down up the stands, and I introduced myself to them. So, Sabie says, oh, yeah. So the guy says, gee, you, the Vanguard used to play at Cav. Oh, and we, and so on. So, he says, well, what are you doing now? I says, I'm just, I'm closing down here. This week. He says, you are? He says, well, listen, this is my bass player. He's got to go back to Boston to go to the Navy. They, they drafted me in the Army, see. The Navy. So, he says, would you, would you like to take the job or come sit in with you, stay with us? We have two more weeks here before we leave, see. I says, well, I says, I said, well, maybe I would. He says, I'll let you know. He says, well, we're having a rehearsal tomorrow. Would you come down and rehearse with us? I says, yes, gladly. And he says, no. He says, stay in there, play a set with us. I said, well, all right. And I sat in with them and played a set, and man, and so they had a lot of music. They had plenty of music. That's all they did was reading, you know, heavy arrangements. For a small group, they played, they sounded like a big band, a big band sound, see. Because they had, they had two trumpets, three saxophones, and three rhythms, see. And baritone, tenor, and alto. That's how these, oh boy, these are really junk. So, so I sat in and played with them. So, and I said, that's wonderful. He says, will you come and make rehearsals with us tomorrow? I says, okay, I'll sit in. Then I started rehearsing with the guys, and so that, that week before the boy, when he left, and I closed down there, and I opened up with him. And I stayed there, I tell you, stay for two weeks, and found when they got ready to go back to Boston, so he asked me to go to Boston. That was the problem then, see. I says, well, I don't want to leave New York. He says, well, would you just, just go to Boston and open up with us, since you play with the band, you'll, you'll, you'll understand it and everything, so just open up with us, stay a week if you don't like it, or you don't have to stay, you know, until we can get somebody, you know, like that, around Boston. I says, well, I says, okay. I said, because going back, and going to Boston, that means I have to, I have to do a lot of things. I brought up a lot of things. I had a nice little apartment and everything, you know. So I had to tear down, and pack up, and go with, with things. So, so when I got there, I went there for one week to stay, and I stayed 18 years. How long? Yeah, 18 years. How did you come out here now? Yeah, well, I come, I come back about a year ago. Yeah. See, when I went back to Boston, and doing, and a little after the war, and after all the boys, and everybody started on this modern jazz and kick, so some of the boys, and feel though that they wasn't, a little bit up on everything that happened, so they, Boston is the greatest field for music, you know, schools, you got all those conservatories. I know Boston, somebody, huh? So, so gee, and I look back and stuff, I say, well, I've been playing a long time, and I said, and I know practically every type of music there is, and coming up during my time, I play. Please.
